entry.evidence: the relative importance of climate simulation as compared with other sources of uncertainty remains unclear

sequences.source_document: Holube et al. 2022, The Cryosphere 16, 315–331 (publisher XML text, with PDF for figures)

steps.action: Authors review earlier Greenland SMB projections forced by subsets of CMIP3, CMIP5 and CMIP6 ESMs with PDD and regional climate models (Graversen, Yan, Fettweis, Hanna, Hofer).
steps.quote: For CMIP6, simulated the SMB of Greenland using the output of five ESMs.

steps.action: Authors pose the question of how ESM choice, emission scenario and snow-model parameters compare as sources of SMB uncertainty.
steps.quote: the relative importance of climate simulation as compared with other sources of uncertainty remains unclear

steps.action: Authors adopt their group's efficient surface energy and mass balance model BESSI on a 10 km Greenland grid, developed in earlier papers.
steps.quote: The Bergen Snow Simulator (BESSI) is a surface energy and mass balance model for glaciated regions with a flexible spatial domain.

steps.action: Authors calibrate BESSI albedo and turbulent-exchange parameters against RACMO SMB (1979–2017) with seven objective functions and take the Pareto optimal set of 16 parameter sets.
steps.quote: we calculate the Pareto optimal set

steps.action: Authors select 26 CMIP6 ESMs and the four Tier 1 SSP scenarios and bias-correct ESM inputs against ERA-Interim with the delta method (precipitation by monthly ratio).
steps.quote: We selected 26 ESMs that provide all of BESSI's input variables for at least two scenarios

steps.action: Authors describe the bias-corrected ESM input variables over the ice sheet: rising temperature, dew point, longwave and precipitation, falling shortwave, with weak precipitation trends relative to inter-ESM spread.
steps.quote: The trends in precipitation are weaker compared to the ranges of values between the ESMs.

steps.action: Authors design the main ensemble (96 ESM–scenario combinations plus 26 historical runs, each with 16 parameter sets) and a single-forcing ensemble for SSP585 with one transient variable at a time.
steps.quote: resulting in 1952 simulations

steps.action: Authors run the ensemble and report median SMB declining in all scenarios, more strongly with higher emissions (median −226 Gt/yr in SSP585 by 2091–2100), with inter-ESM spread growing with forcing.
steps.quote: The surface mass balance decreases relative to the historical simulations in all scenarios

steps.action: Authors check the simplified ice-flow correction for melted ice against neglecting ice flow and report a difference below 40 Gt/yr (appendix).
steps.quote: The difference amounts to less than 40 Gt yr - 1 for all scenarios

steps.action: Authors compare ERA-Interim-forced and historical-ESM-forced SMB and attribute the early-21st-century low SMB in reanalysis to Greenland blocking poorly represented in ESMs.
steps.quote: A similar reduction in SMB is not observed when forcing BESSI with historical ESM data

steps.action: Authors map end-of-century SMB anomalies, inter-ESM standard deviation and equilibrium lines, finding largest decrease in the west and largest relative spread near the equilibrium line.
steps.quote: the choice of ESM is decisive for the SMB in this region

steps.action: Authors partition ensemble variance (Hawkins and Sutton, fourth-degree polynomial fits, law of total variance, ESMs weighted by historical skill) into ESM, scenario, parameter and internal-variability components.
steps.quote: At the end of the century, the ESM uncertainty is about 62 % and the scenario uncertainty is about 35 %

steps.action: Authors test the partition with 10 realizations of ACCESS-ESM1-5 (attribution bias up to 35% early, small by 2100) and with alternative decompositions Eqs. C5 and C6 (appendix).
steps.quote: the ESM uncertainty is robustly shown to be greater than the scenario uncertainty

steps.action: Authors apply the variance partition to every grid cell for mid- and end-century decades, finding ESM uncertainty dominant over most of the ice sheet.
steps.quote: The separation of variances can be generalized to every grid cell of the GrIS.

steps.action: Authors run single-forcing simulations and find temperature and precipitation have the largest effect and largest inter-ESM spread on SMB, shortwave negligible.
steps.quote: Consequently, these variables dominate the uncertainty of the SMB simulations.

steps.action: Authors set the negligible shortwave effect against Hofer et al. (2017) and explain the mismatch by ESMs' projected shortwave decrease and poor blocking representation.
steps.quote: Shortwave radiation alone has a negligible influence on the SMB in the idealized experiments performed.

steps.action: Authors note the sum of single-forcing changes differs from the fully transient run and refine the explanation of growing spread to non-linear interactions among forcings.
steps.quote: This highlights non-linearities that amplify the SMB reduction.

steps.action: Authors partition variance and single-forcing response for west, north and east regions, finding scenario dependence in the west, temperature-driven ESM spread in the north and precipitation-driven ESM spread in the east.
steps.quote: the ESM uncertainty is mostly a precipitation uncertainty

steps.action: Authors compare results with ISMIP6, MAR forced by the same five CMIP6 ESMs (Hanna et al. 2020) and MAR CMIP3/CMIP5 runs (Fettweis 2008, 2013), finding qualitative agreement, higher BESSI SMB and a spread over three times larger.
steps.quote: we find that in four out of five cases BESSI simulates a higher SMB than MAR

steps.action: Authors keep the claim, after listing caveats (structural model uncertainty, fixed topography, blocking, bias correction), that ESM choice is the largest source of SMB projection uncertainty, and recommend skill-weighting ESMs.
steps.quote: the ESM uncertainty is the largest source of error in the future projections of the GrIS SMB

end.claim: By the end of the 21st century the choice of ESM accounts for about 62% of Greenland SMB projection variance, emission scenario about 35%, and snow-model parameters plus internal variability about 3%, making ESM uncertainty the largest source of SMB uncertainty.

decisive_move.sentence: The Hawkins–Sutton variance partition applied to the 1952-member BESSI ensemble over 26 CMIP6 ESMs produces the headline shares; without it there is no ranking of uncertainty sources.

gates.evidence: The ensemble was designed from a question about uncertainty shares, not a stated hypothesis (§1 ¶3; §2.3 ¶1). The ESM-dominance claim faced a check that could have failed: the ACCESS-ESM1-5 realization test could have shown ESM spread to be internal variability, and it did so for early decades (up to 35%) but not at the end of the century (§3.2 ¶3); alternative decompositions were also compared (§Appendix C ¶4). Nothing is reported as fixed before the simulations.

imports.item: Law of total variance for splitting ensemble variance into components
Pareto optimal set across seven objective functions for parameter calibration

novelty_claims.quote: In our ensemble, the range of uncertainty in the SMB is greater than in previous studies that used fewer ESMs as forcing.
the high numerical efficiency of BESSI enables a more comprehensive analysis of model uncertainty, for example by extending the ESM pool to 26

limits:
No review file or open discussion was supplied, so no review sequence is coded. The paper says it was revised after two anonymous referees (Acknowledgements), but what changed is unknown. Neither novelty statement uses 'first'; both are comparative claims of breadth. Composition is none_fits: the walk is a question-driven model-ensemble uncertainty partition with no rivals, no crucial test, no found conditions and no forecast scored against outcomes. Inference: it is closest to an estimation design enabled by an inherited efficient capability (BESSI). Parameter uncertainty covers only albedo and turbulent-exchange parameters; structural snow-model uncertainty is not sampled, and the authors say so (§3.2 ¶2; §4 ¶5). The realization test used one ESM only, because multiple realizations exist for about half of the ESMs (§3.2 ¶3). Projections cannot be checked against observations. Further caveats the authors acknowledge:
- No ESM quality control beyond bias correction (§4 ¶2).
- Fixed topography, with about 10% bias by 2100 (§4 ¶5).
- Missing diurnal cycle (§4 ¶5).
- Blocking poorly represented (§4 ¶5).
- Bias correction that shrinks inter-ESM spread (§4 ¶5).
- Ice-flow simplification not addressed further (§Appendix A ¶4).
Sub-claims at other statuses:
- Regional patterns (west melt, north late non-linear decrease, east precipitation-driven): estimate_with_resolution.
- The non-linear interaction explanation for growing spread and the blocking explanation of the ERA-Interim versus ESM difference: best_explanation.
- The statement that a narrower ESM selection could reduce uncertainty: explicitly speculation (§4 ¶2), status none.
The calibration step (§2.1 ¶3) may partly reuse earlier work (Zolles et al. 2019); coding it as performed here is an inference.

disagreements.target: Hofer et al. (2017), link between amplified melt and recent increases in shortwave radiation
disagreements.support: Single-forcing runs show negligible shortwave influence; the authors attribute the mismatch to ESMs projecting decreasing shortwave and misrepresenting Greenland blocking.
disagreements.quote: Shortwave radiation alone has a negligible influence on the SMB in the idealized experiments performed.

disagreements.target: Hanna et al. (2020), MAR forced by five CMIP6 ESMs
disagreements.support: For the same five ESMs BESSI gives higher SMB in four cases (attributed to BESSI's known positive bias), and the full 26-ESM spread is over three times larger; four of the five MAR-forcing ESMs have above-average ECS.
disagreements.quote: we find that in four out of five cases BESSI simulates a higher SMB than MAR

disagreements.target: Fettweis et al. (2008), MAR CMIP3 A1B projection with multilinear regression
disagreements.support: Their smaller uncertainty range is attributed to the linear regression omitting non-linear effects and to smaller inter-model differences in CMIP3.
disagreements.quote: It also shows an approximately linear decrease in SMB but with a smaller uncertainty range than in our moderate SSP245 scenario simulation with BESSI.

disagreements.target: Studies projecting SMB from a subset of CMIP ESMs without assessing their quality
disagreements.support: ESM uncertainty is shown to dominate, so selecting few ESMs underestimates spread.
disagreements.quote: studies that only include a subset of the plausible climate projections and do not quantify the quality of these selected representations may produce an incomplete [...]

alternatives_considered.reason: C8–C10 compute expectation values of variances between scenarios, but scenarios should differ because of different external forcing

alternatives_considered.chosen: Precipitation bias correction by ratio of monthly means
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Additive difference; ratio of daily means
alternatives_considered.reason: Difference would give negative values given high variability; daily means affected by individual intense events

alternatives_considered.chosen: Monthly ERA-Interim precipitation climatology redistributed by ESM daily distribution in single-forcing runs
alternatives_considered.reason: Daily climatology overestimates surface albedo through unrealistic daily small snowfall, overestimating mass balance by up to 40%

alternatives_considered.chosen: SSP585 with the best-calibrated parameter set for single-forcing runs
alternatives_considered.reason: SSP585 is available for all 26 ESMs; parameter set gives best results in calibration with RACMO

alternatives_considered.chosen: Same initialized firn cover for every parameter set
Simplified steady-state ice-flow correction for melted ice
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Neglecting ice flow; fully dynamical ice sheet model
alternatives_considered.reason: Grid cells with thin ice distort mass balance when already-melted ice is counted

alternatives_considered.chosen: Restrict analysis to grid cells with at least 50 m ice
alternatives_considered.reason: Exclude snow caps; velocity cannot be assumed constant in thinner ice
Multiple realizations available for only about half of the ESMs

alternatives_considered.chosen: 16 BESSI parameter sets to represent snow-model uncertainty
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Repeating simulations with every SMB model of Fettweis et al. (2020)
alternatives_considered.reason: Computational requirements of some SMB models too high for several hundred simulations

alternatives_considered.chosen: ESMs weighted by historical-period skill against ERA-Interim in the variance split
alternatives_considered.reason: Give more weight to ESMs that perform well in the historical period
